holidays.name: Bathtub Party Day
holidays.description: A bubbly observance encouraging people to turn their bathtub into a personal party zone, complete with bubbles, rubber duckies, snacks, and maybe a beverage or two.
holidays.origin: Bathtub Party Day is an unofficial, folksy holiday with murky origins. It is often linked to the end of Prohibition on December 5, 1933, when the 21st Amendment was ratified, since people had been making bathtub gin during the dry years.
holidays.funFact: The term 'bathtub gin' came from the fact that bottles were often too tall to fit under a sink faucet, so people topped off the homemade booze with water from the bathtub tap.

holidays.name: Repeal Day
holidays.description: A toast-worthy occasion celebrating the end of Prohibition in the United States, when the nation's ban on alcohol was finally lifted.
holidays.origin: On December 5, 1933, Utah became the 36th state to ratify the 21st Amendment, which repealed the 18th Amendment and ended nationwide Prohibition after nearly 14 years.
holidays.funFact: The 21st Amendment is the only amendment in US history that was ratified by state conventions instead of state legislatures, and the only one that repealed another amendment.

holidays.name: Krampusnacht
holidays.description: A spooky night in Alpine folklore when the horned, hairy, chain-rattling Krampus roams the streets to punish naughty children, the dark counterpart to Saint Nicholas.
holidays.origin: Krampusnacht comes from Central European traditions in Austria, Bavaria, Hungary, Slovenia, and nearby regions. It is celebrated on the eve of St. Nicholas Day, December 6, and has roots that may reach back to pre-Christian winter customs.
holidays.funFact: In many towns, groups of locals dress as Krampus in giant carved wooden masks in a Krampuslauf, or Krampus run, and some participants have been known to playfully swat spectators with bundles of birch twigs.

holidays.name: Special Kids Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate children with special needs, encouraging people to recognize their unique talents, resilience, and joy, and to make the world more inclusive.
holidays.origin: Special Kids Day is observed on the first Friday of December by some organizations, but it is also commonly noted on December 5 in lists of awareness days. It grew out of grassroots efforts to promote acceptance and appreciation for kids with disabilities.
holidays.funFact: Many families and schools mark the day with sensory-friendly activities, such as quiet craft sessions and music games designed so every child can take part.

holidays.name: International Ninja Day
holidays.description: A stealthy salute to shadowy warriors, when fans are encouraged to dress in black, sneak up on friends silently, and perhaps leave a few mysterious surprises.
holidays.origin: International Ninja Day is an internet-era unofficial holiday said to be celebrated on December 5, inspired by the legendary spies and assassins of feudal Japan known as shinobi.
holidays.funFact: The popular image of ninjas in all-black outfits probably comes from stagehands in Japanese theater called kuroko, who wore black to signal they were invisible to the audience.
